intro: If you have to come and work, take care of business, or stop over around Laem Chabang port and the industrial estates in the Si Racha area, and you want something more than a plain budget hotel — a pool to soak in after work, a gym, a restaurant, and easy parking, all at a price that's still kind to your wallet — Avana Laemchabang Boutique Hotel is a name people around here mention a lot · it's a 4-star boutique hotel of around 100 rooms down Soi Laemthong 2 in Thung Sukhla, Si Racha district, and it leans on a saltwater pool, clean spacious rooms, and a location near the port and the industrial estate rather than being a beachfront resort like the ones in Bang Saen or Pattaya · it isn't right by the beach and the location is fairly quiet, tucked deep down a lane, but it gives you more amenities than the price suggests, service that a lot of guests praise, and convenience for people coming here for work or passing through · prices start at about THB 654/night · real-guest review scores run around 8.0–8.3 across hundreds of reviews on Agoda and Trip.com

body.html: Overview and who it suits — if we had to sum up what this place is in one sentence, Avana Laemchabang Boutique Hotel is "a hotel with 4-star amenities at budget-hotel prices, for people who have a reason to be around Laem Chabang" rather than a place built directly for a seaside holiday · it's a boutique hotel with around 100 rooms, open since about 2013, down Soi Laemthong 2, Moo 10, Thung Sukhla, Si Racha district, Chonburi province, in an area ringed by Laem Chabang port, industrial estates, and Laem Chabang Public Park · what sets Avana apart from the usual budget hotels in the same area is that it has an outdoor saltwater pool, a kids' pool, a gym, a restaurant, and spa services all in one place, even though prices still start in the few-hundred-baht range · pulling together what real reviews say, the people this place suits best are business travellers and staff coming to work or hold meetings around the Laem Chabang industrial estate, people who work with the port, ship crew stopping over before boarding, families who want a spacious room with a pool for the kids, and travellers who drive through and want a bed for one night with a pool and easy parking · on the flip side, if you're after sea views, sand to stroll along, or a holiday-resort feel in the middle of the tourist action, this isn't the answer, and you should look past it to Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · put simply, Avana sells well-rounded amenities, spacious rooms, and a location near the workplaces — not a beachfront vibe or full-blown luxury

Location and getting around — Avana sits at 114/99 Soi Laemthong 2, Moo 10, Thung Sukhla, Si Racha, an area tied to the industrial and logistics economy of eastern Chonburi · the strength of this location is that it's near Laem Chabang port and the Laem Chabang Industrial Estate, just a few minutes' drive away, which makes it very convenient for people here on business · neighbourhood green space like Laem Chabang Public Park is only about 430 m away, and Wat Laem Chabang (the newly built one) is about 770 m away, a short walk or drive · Pattaya beach, the main tourist draw, is about 25–30 min drive away, and U-Tapao Airport is about 58 km away · one thing we have to say plainly, based on real reviews, is that the hotel sits down a fairly deep lane that's not easy to find the first time — many reviews from foreign guests say it's hard to find without GPS or without asking locals, and there aren't restaurants and convenience stores right next door the way there are in an in-town neighbourhood · anyone driving in by car will have the easiest time, since there's free private parking, while those without a car should have a plan for getting out to find food or into Si Racha town, because taxis and ride-hailing apps in this area can be harder to get at certain times than in town · overall Avana's location works well for people working in the industrial estate and those driving themselves, but it isn't a location you can explore on foot as a general tourist

"The room was bigger than I expected, clean, with a comfy bed, and there's a pool to use in the evening. The price is really good value for what you get. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the location is close to my workplace in the industrial estate, just a few minutes' drive. If I'm working around Laem Chabang again I'll come back and stay."

Room types and decor — Avana's rooms go for simple contemporary; they're not luxurious, but the point a lot of guests agree on is that the rooms are bigger than the price suggests · the main room types break down into the Premier Single Room, a compact King-bed room (some rooms have no window, so check before booking if you want natural light), the Premier 3-Bed Room for groups of colleagues or families, the Executive Room at around 28 sqm which is roomier and usually on floors 2–4 of the building, and the largest, the Junior Suite, for those who want more space · every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge/minibar, a safe, free Wi-Fi, and an en-suite bathroom · most real reviews praise the rooms as clean, with comfy beds, good water pressure in the bathroom, and usable space beyond what the price implies · but there are some points worth knowing, told straight — some reviews say the rooms look older in person than in the promotional photos posted on the booking sites, some fittings are starting to show their age, a few voices mention power sockets that are loose or don't feel secure, which is something to watch for and to tell the hotel about if you run into it, and the soundproofing between rooms isn't great, so set your expectations at the level of a budget boutique hotel with spacious, clean rooms rather than a brand-new, flawless property

Amenities, pool, and spa — this is where Avana has the edge over hotels at a similar price around Laem Chabang, because it has a real, working outdoor saltwater pool plus a separate kids' pool, which is something you don't often find at hotels starting in the few-hundred-baht range around here · several reviews praise the pool as clean and a good spot to relax in after work, and families with kids feel more at ease with a kids' pool to play in · besides the pool there's a gym, the Avana Cafe restaurant, a bar/lounge, and Thai massage and aromatherapy spa services for anyone who wants to unwind after a long day's work · for the basics there's 24-hour room service, laundry service, free luggage storage, a 24-hour front desk, concierge service, free Wi-Fi, and free private parking, which helps a lot for people driving themselves · there's also garden space on the grounds to sit and get some air · we should say plainly that the pool and gym here are city-hotel sized, not a big resort-style pool by the sea, and they're more for soaking and cooling off than for serious lap swimming, but in value-for-money terms at this price, having a pool, gym, and spa in one place is clearly a step above the budget competitors in the same area

Food and dining — Avana has an on-site restaurant called Avana Cafe that serves mainly breakfast and lunch, which helps a lot since the location is fairly quiet and outside restaurants aren't right next to the hotel · many real reviews mention a buffet breakfast that's filling and good value, with both Thai and international options, a point guests here on business say is convenient because they can eat and head straight out to work · to be straight about it, though, some reviews note that the restaurant focuses mainly on breakfast, dinner options in the hotel may be limited, and the menu details and opening hours may change from time to time, so it's worth confirming when you book if dinner in the hotel matters to you · for other meals, people driving themselves can head out to made-to-order eateries, seafood restaurants, and convenience stores in Thung Sukhla and Si Racha town, which aren't far, including the famous Si Racha seafood and seaside seafood spots that are a short drive away · overall, food at Avana isn't a reason to eat in the hotel for every meal, but having a restaurant and good-value breakfast helps with convenience for people who are worn out from work and don't want to go anywhere in the morning

Service and staff — service is a point where Avana earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews, and it's one reason the overall score holds up well · many guests say the staff are smiling, friendly, attentive, and willing to help, and some reviews mention that the team helped sort out transport and recommended restaurants in the area · for guests here on business and tired from travelling, finding a team that checks you in quickly and is ready to help is worth a lot · but for balance, we have to say plainly that a few voices in the reviews note that some staff have limited English, which can be a minor hurdle for foreign guests, and some mention occasional building-systems issues, such as power dips or a lift that's out of service at times · overall, though, service is still a strong point here, and it's part of what helps lift the overall experience even though the building isn't new

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling together Agoda, Trip.com, Tripadvisor, and various review sources, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: rooms spacious and clean beyond the price, comfy beds, good water pressure; a saltwater pool and kids' pool that are hard to find at this price; a filling, good-value buffet breakfast; smiling, friendly, helpful staff; free, roomy parking; and excellent value relative to the amenities you get · many guests here on business say they'll come back and stay again when they're in the area · On the gripes side: the most talked-about issue is that the location is down a deep lane, hard to find the first time, and far from restaurants and tourist spots, making it tricky to get around for people without a car · next is that some rooms and parts of the building look older than in the photos, with some fittings starting to show their age; a few voices mention loose power sockets and soundproofing between rooms that isn't great · on top of that there's the restaurant leaning on breakfast with limited dinner options, the limited English of some staff, and tour groups checking in on some evenings making the common areas busier than usual · most of these gripes can be handled by setting the right expectations, using GPS to navigate, and driving yourself, rather than being problems that make the place unstayable

"Great value for this price — you get both a spacious room and a pool, and it suits people coming to work around the industrial estate. The one downside is that it's down a deep lane that's hard to find the first time, so you need GPS, and the restaurants are far enough that you have to drive out. But if you're here for work, the value on both price and amenities is real."

Price and value — nightly room rates start at about THB 654/night for a Premier room on weekdays when you book online, rising to around THB 900–THB 1,500 for an Executive room or Junior Suite, or during periods with events or activities around Laem Chabang · what makes Avana good value is that you get a spacious room, a saltwater pool, a gym, a restaurant, and free parking at a price close to budget hotels without a pool in the same area · compared with an upper-tier chain hotel in Laem Chabang–Si Racha like Holiday Inn & Suites Siracha Laemchabang, which is newer and has more complete amenities but costs several times more, Avana loses on newness and chain standards but wins on price and value for those who want a spacious room with a pool on a limited budget · and compared with other budget hotels around Laem Chabang like NYTH Hotel, which starts at about 545 baht but has no pool, Avana has a clear edge on the pool and amenities, in exchange for a slightly higher price and a location that's harder to find · in short, if you put weight on having a pool, a spacious room, and value on a limited budget, every baht you pay comes back to you well

What to know before you book — there are several things that help make the stay smoother · one, the location is down Soi Laemthong 2, which is fairly deep and hard to find the first time, so turn on GPS and save the coordinates in advance, especially if you arrive at night · two, some room types like the Premier Single may have no window, so if you want natural light or a view, specify and ask when booking · three, some rooms and parts of the building look older than in the promotional photos, so set your expectations at the level of a budget boutique hotel with spacious rooms and a pool, not a new hotel, and if you find a loose socket or broken fitting, tell the hotel right away · four, the location is fairly quiet and restaurants are far, so if you don't have a car, plan for getting out to find food or use the hotel's restaurant/room service · five, the restaurant focuses mainly on breakfast, so if dinner in the hotel matters to you, confirm beforehand · six, if you're coming mainly to visit Pattaya, this location is about 25–30 min drive away, so weigh up whether the pool and budget price are worth it, or choose to stay closer to the tourist spots instead · seven, during periods with events or activities in the industrial estate, rooms can fill up fast, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms

The bottom line — from everything real reviews say, Avana Laemchabang Boutique Hotel is the best fit for people coming for work or passing through the Laem Chabang–Si Racha area who want a spacious, clean room with a pool to relax in and easy parking, at a price that's still affordable · having a saltwater pool, a kids' pool, a gym, a restaurant, and a spa at prices starting in the few-hundred-baht range, plus friendly service and rooms that are bigger than the price, makes it good value for business travellers, industrial-estate staff, ship crew, families with kids, and travellers driving themselves · but you have to accept, honestly, that it's down a deep lane that's hard to find the first time, it's not by the beach, it's far from restaurants and tourist spots, some rooms and parts of the building are starting to show their age and look older than in the photos, and there are minor gripes about soundproofing and the language of some staff · if you're looking for a sea-view resort or a holiday vibe in the middle of the tourist action, this isn't the answer, and you should look at options on the Bang Saen or Pattaya side instead · but for a practical stay coming to work or stopping over around Laem Chabang, where you want a spacious room with a pool and value on a limited budget — Avana meets that need well, and that's why it has held a solid review score in this area for so long

honestSummary: Avana Laemchabang Boutique Hotel is a good-value option for people who are coming for work or passing through the Laem Chabang–Si Racha area and want a spacious, clean room with a pool to relax in and easy parking, at a price that's still affordable — a saltwater pool, a kids' pool, a gym, a restaurant, and a spa at prices starting in the few-hundred-baht range · but you have to accept that the location is down a deep lane that's hard to find the first time, it's not by the beach, it's far from restaurants and tourist spots, and some rooms look older than in the photos
honestChecks: If you don't have your own car — the hotel is down Soi Laemthong 2, which is fairly deep and hard to find, restaurants and tourist spots are far, and taxis and ride-hailing apps can be hard to get at certain times → plan to use the hotel's restaurant/room service, or arrange a rental car

If you want a sea-view resort or a holiday vibe — this is a hotel in an industrial area; it has a pool but it's not by the beach and there's no sea view → if you're focused on the sea and a relaxing vibe, try a resort on the Bang Saen or Pattaya side like Centara Grand Mirage or The Tide Resort instead

If you're worried about how new the rooms are — some rooms and parts of the building look older than in the promotional photos, and a few voices mention loose power sockets and soundproofing that isn't great → ask for a recently renovated room, set your expectations on spaciousness and value above all, and tell the hotel right away if you find a broken fitting

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Avana Laemchabang Boutique Hotel

faq.q: Where is Avana Laemchabang Boutique Hotel · how close is it to Laem Chabang port?
faq.a: The hotel is at 114/99 Soi Laemthong 2, Moo 10, Thung Sukhla, Si Racha district, Chonburi · it's near Laem Chabang port and the Laem Chabang Industrial Estate, just a few minutes' drive away · Laem Chabang Public Park is about 430 m away, and Wat Laem Chabang is about 770 m away · Pattaya beach is about 25–30 min drive away, and U-Tapao Airport is about 58 km · one thing to know is that the hotel is down a deep lane, so turn on GPS to navigate

faq.q: Does Avana Laemchabang Boutique Hotel have a pool?
faq.a: It has an outdoor saltwater pool with a kids' pool · it's the standout that gives Avana an edge over hotels at a similar price around Laem Chabang, most of which have no pool · besides the pool there's a gym and Thai/aroma massage spa services · ideal for people who want a place with a pool to relax in after work or to bring the kids for a swim, at an affordable price

faq.q: What's the starting price at Avana Laemchabang · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 654/night for a Premier room when you book online on a weekday · there are Premier Single (some rooms have no window), Premier 3-Bed, Executive at around 28 sqm, and Junior Suite rooms · prices rise to around THB 900–1,500 depending on the room type and period · we recommend booking through online platforms and comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com before booking

faq.q: Who does Avana Laemchabang suit best?
faq.a: It suits business travellers, staff coming to work around the Laem Chabang industrial estate, people who work with the port, ship crew, families who want a spacious room with a pool for the kids, and travellers driving themselves who want complete amenities at a budget price · it doesn't suit people who want a sea-view resort or a holiday vibe in the middle of the tourist action, who should consider the Bang Saen or Pattaya side instead

faq.q: Is it convenient to get to Avana Laemchabang without a car?
faq.a: The hotel is down Soi Laemthong 2, which is fairly deep and hard to find the first time, and restaurants and convenience stores aren't right next door, so without your own car it's harder to get around than in an in-town area, and taxis and ride-hailing apps can be hard to get at certain times · there's free private parking for people driving themselves · those without a car should plan to use the hotel's restaurant and room service, or arrange a rental car

faq.q: Does Avana Laemchabang have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: Yes · the hotel has the Avana Cafe restaurant serving a buffet breakfast that many reviews praise as filling and good value, with both Thai and international options, open mainly for breakfast and lunch (dinner options in the hotel may be limited) · there's free private parking and free Wi-Fi, ideal for people driving themselves · plus 24-hour room service and laundry service
